summary: DoH fallback to TCP blocked by corporate proxy leading to stale KV cache and model pull slowdowns in private deployment
summary_detail: Customer reports recurring slowdowns on model inference for a private VPC deployment. Investigation points to DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) UDP->TCP fallback being dropped by an on-premises corporate proxy, causing control-plane DNS resolution delays and subsequent KV cache staleness on serving nodes.
description:
Issue summary:
- Customers (ArchimedesHealth, private deployment in us-east-1) observed recurring 500/502 model requests and elevated P95 latency for streaming responses starting 2026-03-04 22:00 UTC. Failures coincide with long control-plane name resolution times and repeated model-shard fetch retries.

Impact:
- Intermittent model generation timeouts for a small percentage (~3-5%) of requests; sustained P95 latency spike from 280ms -> 1.8s. Some legacy clients experienced streaming connection resets.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC peered to Redwood control plane), serving nodes in us-east-1, control-plane endpoints behind vpce, egress via corporate HTTP proxy appliance.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From a serving node inside customer VPC, run: dig +tcp @resolver.example.local model-cache.redwood.internal A and measure latency.
2) Trigger a high-frequency small-sequence inference workload (~200 qps) to force model-shard pulls.
3) Observe control-plane DNS fallbacks, repeated model GET retries, and KV cache misses on serving nodes.

Observed behavior:
- DNS queries normally attempt UDP DoH; when truncated, clients fall back to TCP. The corporate proxy performs UDP-to-TCP downgrade/translation but silently drops or times out these TCP fallback attempts for some names. This causes DNS resolution to stall ~6-12s before retry/backoff and triggers artifact fetch retries from the serving runtime.
- Serving nodes report KV cache staleness warnings and increased read-after-miss requests to control plane; model shard downloads move from parallel fast paths to serialized retries causing increased tail latency.

Expected behavior:
- DoH fallback to TCP should succeed (or fail quickly) and not cause multi-second stalls; serving runtime should be able to refresh KV cache in sub-second windows.

Relevant logs and traces:
- Control plane logs: repeated name resolution timeouts for resolver.example.local at 2026-03-04T22:03:12Z (tcp fallback timeout 10s).
- Serving node debug: "kv_cache: miss; model_shard_fetch retry_count=3; http get timeout 12000ms"
- tcpdump capture (attached link) shows TLS ClientHello over TCP followed by RST with no TLS handshake completion.

Temporary workaround identified:
- Customer applied ACL exception on proxy to allow direct TCP port 53 to resolver for a subset of control-plane names; immediate reduction in stall frequency observed.

Notes:
- Customer is on a private deployment so they manage the egress appliance; changes require change-window approval.
comments: 2026-03-05 09:12 - Samira Khan (Support): Initial report received from ArchimedesHealth via support form. Captured traces and tcpdump attached. Assigned to network on-call.

2026-03-05 10:01 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Reproduced from a test node in customer-like env. Observed DoH UDP responses with TC=1 and subsequent TCP fallback attempts timing out after 10s. Filed INT-4421 to capture proxy behavior on customer side.

2026-03-05 10:45 - Priya Patel (Solutions Eng): Confirmed customer proxy appliance does HTTP CONNECT interception and rewrites ALPN; raised concern that proxy is terminating/inspecting TCP fallback flows and dropping TLS. Provided suggested ACL change to customer to allow direct TCP connections for control-plane resolvers.

2026-03-05 14:30 - Customer (ArchimedesHealth - infra@archmed.io): Applied an ACL exception in test window for resolver.example.local and reported latency returned to baseline for the duration of the window. Asking for permanent mitigations that don't require broad open egress.

2026-03-06 08:12 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Noted correlation with proxy firmware 3.4.8 behavior where UDP->TCP DoH handoff is rewritten to an HTTP proxy flow and ALPN stripped. Recommending two options: (A) Add targeted allow ACLs per resolver + port 853/443 as appropriate, or (B) deploy a local caching resolver inside VPC that translates DoH to internal cache over UDP.

2026-03-07 16:05 - Samira Khan (Support): Scheduling a follow-up runbook session with customer to implement local resolver pattern and to validate long-term fix. Customer requested a short-design doc and runbook from Redwood on recommended architecture for private deployments behind strict HTTP proxies.
investigation_notes: Captured tcpdump on serving node showing ClientHello over TCP followed by immediate RST from proxy without TLS ServerHello. No evidence of certificate being presented.
Proxy appliance logs show a connection attempt rewritten into an intercepted HTTP CONNECT session; ALPN and SNI values were sanitized by proxy policy for non-whitelisted hostnames.
Control-plane health checks show spike in RPS from serving nodes during the timeouts as they retry model shard requests while KV cache is rebuilding.
Tested edge-case: forcing DOH over HTTPS (443) vs DNS-over-TLS (853) shows proxy handles 443-based DoH differently — some 443 flows allowed, others proxied and stripped.
resolution_notes: Interim fix: customer created scoped proxy ACLs allowing direct TCP handoff to resolver.example.local for port 853 and TCP-based DoH fallback paths for control-plane names; observed immediate remediation of stalls.

Recommended long-term: customer to run a small forwarding resolver (e.g., unbound or dnscrypt-proxy) inside the VPC that handles DoH/DoT translation and presents a stable UDP resolver to serving nodes to avoid proxy interference. Provided reference runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/private-deploy-dns-fallback-handling

Platform mitigation: engineering (INT-4421) will add additional timeouts and a fast-fail path in the serving runtime when DNS TCP fallback shows repeated RSTs to avoid long synchronous stalls during model shard fetch phase. Patch PR referenced: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5871

Follow-ups: Solutions Eng to run architecture review with ArchimedesHealth (scheduled 2026-03-10). SRE to monitor control-plane DNS latencies for similar patterns across other private deployments and raise an alert if >1% nodes show TCP fallback RSTs over 24h.
Ticket resolved with customer agreement to implement local resolver; will close when production runbook is applied and 7 days of stable metrics observed.
